controls.title: AI system purpose documented
controls.description: The intended purpose, scope, and use case of the AI system is clearly documented, including whether the system is decision-support, autonomous decision-making, generative, analytical, or operational.

controls.title: Application domain identified
controls.description: The application domain of the AI system is identified and documented (e.g., healthcare, finance, law enforcement, education, transportation, critical infrastructure, entertainment, customer service).

controls.title: AI output type classified
controls.description: The type of AI output is classified: prediction, classification, recommendation, generation (text/image/audio/video/code), translation, detection, optimisation, or control.

controls.title: Autonomy level defined
controls.description: The level of AI autonomy is defined on the spectrum from fully human-controlled to fully autonomous, including human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, and human-out-of-the-loop configurations.

controls.title: Interaction modality documented
controls.description: The interaction modality of the AI system is documented (e.g., conversational/chat, API-driven, embedded, batch processing, real-time streaming, multimodal).

controls.title: Deployment environment documented
controls.description: The deployment environment is documented, including whether the AI system operates in cloud, on-premise, edge, hybrid, or embedded environments.

controls.title: Operational scale characterised
controls.description: The operational scale of the AI system is characterised, including the number of users, transaction volume, geographic distribution, and languages supported.

controls.title: Criticality of use assessed
controls.description: The criticality of the AI use case is assessed based on potential consequences of failure or misuse, including safety-critical, high-stakes, and low-risk classifications.

controls.title: Regulatory context identified
controls.description: The regulatory and legal context applicable to the AI deployment is identified, including sector-specific laws, data protection regulations, export controls, and AI-specific legislation.

controls.title: Integration dependencies mapped
controls.description: Dependencies on upstream data sources, downstream systems, and third-party AI components are mapped and documented.

controls.title: Developers and deployers identified
controls.description: AI developers, operators, and deployers are clearly identified with defined roles and responsibilities throughout the AI lifecycle.

controls.title: End users characterised
controls.description: End users of the AI system are characterised, including their technical sophistication, accessibility needs, cultural context, and potential vulnerability status.

controls.title: Affected populations documented
controls.description: Populations affected by AI decisions but not directly interacting with the system are identified and documented, including third parties and communities.

controls.title: Oversight bodies identified
controls.description: Regulatory bodies, auditors, and oversight entities with jurisdiction over the AI system are identified and engagement mechanisms are established.

controls.title: Training data classified
controls.description: Training data is classified by type (structured, unstructured, synthetic, real-world), sensitivity level (public, internal, confidential, regulated), and provenance (first-party, third-party, open data).

controls.title: Model architecture documented
controls.description: The AI model architecture is documented including model family (neural network, decision tree, ensemble, foundation model, etc.), parameter scale, training paradigm, and fine-tuning approach.

controls.title: Foundation model usage declared
controls.description: Use of foundation models or large pre-trained models (LLMs, vision models, etc.) is declared, including model provenance, version, and any fine-tuning or adaptation applied.

controls.title: Data lineage tracked
controls.description: Data lineage from collection through processing to model training is tracked, enabling traceability of how training data influences model behaviour.

controls.title: Synthetic data usage documented
controls.description: Use of synthetic data in training, evaluation, or augmentation is documented, including generation methodology and validation of representativeness.

controls.title: AI risk tier assigned
controls.description: A risk tier is assigned to the AI system (e.g., minimal, limited, high, unacceptable) based on intended use, potential harm, and deployment context, consistent with applicable regulatory frameworks.

controls.title: Harm taxonomy applied
controls.description: A structured harm taxonomy is applied to identify potential AI-related harms including physical, psychological, financial, societal, reputational, and democratic harms.

controls.title: Dual-use potential assessed
controls.description: The potential for dual-use or misuse of the AI system is assessed, including the possibility that the system's capabilities could be repurposed for harmful applications.

controls.title: Cascading risk dependencies identified
controls.description: Dependencies that could create cascading risks are identified, including interconnected AI systems, critical infrastructure dependencies, and network effects.

controls.title: Accountability structures defined
controls.description: Clear accountability structures are defined for the AI system covering development, deployment, operation, monitoring, and decommissioning phases.

controls.title: Documentation standards applied
controls.description: Standardised documentation is maintained including model cards, datasheets for datasets, system cards, and impact assessments appropriate to the AI system's risk tier.

controls.title: Transparency disclosures made
controls.description: Appropriate transparency disclosures are made to users and affected parties about the use of AI, its capabilities, limitations, and the basis for AI-generated outputs.

controls.title: Contestability mechanisms in place
controls.description: Mechanisms are in place for users and affected parties to contest AI-generated decisions, request human review, and seek redress.

controls.title: Lifecycle governance documented
controls.description: Governance processes covering the full AI lifecycle — from conception and development through deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning — are documented and implemented.
